item.title: Spain to vote in election that could put far right in power for first time since Franco
item.description:
After eight years of socialist-led government, Spain is at a crossroads. Can Pedro Sánchez pull off another electoral comeback, or will the conservative Partido Popular make way for the far right into national government for the first time since the end of Franco's 40-year brutal reign? Just back from Madrid, Richard Werly, Europe correspondent for the Swiss daily Blick, joins Angela Diffley to examine the final days of campaigning and the generational divisions shaping Sunday’s snap elections. The youth are divided between the left and the far-right Vox party. Sánchez, nicknamed the “Teflon politician”, has campaigned heavily on housing and social issues. “We may see an outgoing prime minister performing better than expected,” says Werly.

Sources: Al Jazeera English, France 24, Semafor, The Guardian

item.title: Canada's Supreme Court largely upholds a Quebec ban on religious symbols for public servants
item.description:
Closely watched decision exposes tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights Canada’s top court has largely upheld a controversial secularism law in the province of Quebec barring public sector workers from wearing conspicuous religious symbols, in a closely watched decision that exposes the tensions between minority rights and the power of government to override those rights. In a 6-1 ruling released on Friday morning , the supreme court found Quebec was permitted to shield the law, Bill 21, from most court challenges on the grounds that it violated charter rights. item.title: Open Thread
item.description:
People share food at the dinner table during Thanksgiving. —Stock photo—Getty Images As households across America prepare to gather for their Thanksgiving celebrations , there’s one question at the forefront of hosts’ minds: what time should dinner be served? A quick glance on social media will tell you that it’s a hotly-debated topic, and one that people have firm opinions on. Lifestyle expert Martha Stewart’s online publication conducted a poll in 2024, asking readers what time Thanksgiving dinner should start. More than 34,000 people joined the conversation, with the majority of respondents (13,586) saying the meal should begin between 2 to 3 p.m., local time. Stewart is also a proponent of these timings, telling the Today show last year that she believes dinner should be served at 2 p.m., as “people are hungry” and are likely already starting to “circle the kitchen.” But preferences…

item.title: Taiwan awaits local election results as China watches
item.description:
Taiwanese officials raise alarm over interference by China in elections that will shape fortunes of ruling party Taiwanese voters go to the polls on Saturday in closely watched local elections that will shape the fortunes of the ruling Democratic Progressive party (DPP) as it navigates an increasingly precarious set of relationships on the global stage. Saturday’s vote will choose mayors, council members and other local leaders across 22 districts. Unlike the presidential elections, in which foreign policy is often a key issue, the local elections, held every four years , are largely focused on bread-and-butter issues such as housing affordability and wealth distribution.
